name: Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome due to Paternal Uniparental Disomy of Chromosome 11
aliases: Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome with paternal uniparental disomy

criteria.description: Lateralized overgrowth (hemihyperplasia) of one side of the body
Abdominal wall defects such as omphalocele or umbilical hernia
Molecular confirmation of paternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 11p15

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least three major criteria or two major criteria plus molecular confirmation of paternal UPD of chromosome 11p15
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing for imprinting defects or UPD is essential for confirmation

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic enlarged tongue causing feeding and breathing difficulties
Asymmetric overgrowth of one side of the body or limbs
searchTerms: unequal body size on one side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abdominal wall defects (omphalocele or umbilical hernia)
searchTerms: belly wall defect with organs outside

common.notes: Low blood sugar in the neonatal period requiring treatment
Enlargement of liver, kidneys, or pancreas
searchTerms: big liver, spleen, or other organs

common.symptomName: Increased risk of embryonal tumors (e.g., Wilms tumor)
searchTerms: more likely to develop embryonal tumors
too much amniotic fluid in pregnancy
excess fluid around fetus before birth
low blood sugar after newborn period

rare.notes: Hearing impairment due to nerve dysfunction

imaging: Abdominal ultrasound showing organomegaly and tumor surveillance
MRI or CT for tumor detection (e.g., Wilms tumor)
genetic: Molecular confirmation of paternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 11p15
Methylation analysis showing loss of maternal imprinting at 11p15
other: Physical examination revealing macroglossia and hemihyperplasia
Tumor surveillance protocols due to increased cancer risk

distinguishingFeatures: Distinct facial features including coarse face and supernumerary nipples
Characteristic facial gestalt with prominent forehead

redFlags: Rapid abdominal mass growth suggestive of Wilms tumor
Severe neonatal hypoglycemia refractory to treatment
Airway obstruction due to macroglossia causing respiratory distress
references: Weksberg R, Shuman C, Beckwith JB. Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome. Eur J Hum Genet. 2010;18(1):8-14.
Brioude F, et al. Expert consensus document: Clinical and molecular diagnosis, screening and management of Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2018;14(4):229-249.
Orphanet: Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome due to paternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 11 (ORPHA:96193).
